state.body: At 02:14 UTC our SIEM flagged 47 failed logins against the customer-portal account belonging to user id 88213, immediately followed by one successful login from 203.0.113.10, a known Tor exit node. Within four minutes that session created a new API token, changed the account's notification email to a protonmail address, and disabled SMS two-factor authentication. The account's login history for the prior 90 days is exclusively Auckland and Wellington; this successful auth geolocated to Frankfurt. We force-expired all sessions at 02:31, revoked the new token, and locked the account pending owner verification. During the window the attacker did view the account's own profile page and its billing summary (last four digits of the card only). I pulled the DLP and database-access logs carefully: there is no evidence any bulk export ran, no PII table was queried beyond that single account record, and no other customers' data was touched. Root cause looks like credential reuse - the same password appears in a 2023 third-party breach corpus we subscribe to. My read is this was targeted credential stuffing that succeeded against one account, not a platform-wide breach. Recommendations: (1) force a password reset for this user, (2) require a stronger second factor before restoring access, (3) notify the user per our 72-hour policy, and (4) sweep the breach corpus against active users for other reused passwords. There is no sign of malware on our side, no lateral movement, and nothing pointing to an insider. Customer-facing impact is limited to this one account, which is now locked. I'm classifying this as a confirmed account compromise: high severity but contained. Full timeline, raw auth logs, and the DLP report are attached. Paging the on-call IR lead for the user-notification decision. - SOC Analyst, Tier 2
